output.entity_proposed: National Native Flower Parks Council (the Council)
output.proposal: HB No. 11304 seeks to establish a national system of Native Flower Parks, creating for this purpose a National Native Flower Parks Council attached to the DENR and a Native Flower Parks Development Fund, to promote the conservation, propagation and public appreciation of Philippine native and endemic flowering plants.
output.alignment: As a government organization measure, the review should examine whether the proposed Council, attached to the DENR as the policy-making, standard-setting and coordinating body for Native Flower Parks, duplicates functions already exercised by the DENR-Biodiversity Management Bureau, the Protected Area Management Boards, the National Parks Development Committee, the Department of Tourism and its attached agencies, and local government units, and how its creation relates to the streamlining of the Executive branch and the reduction of overlapping functions under the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231). The review should also assess the creation of a trust fund alongside a separate General Appropriations Act line item, and the proposed release of a portion of the TIEZA share in travel tax collections to the Fund. No matching priority area in the FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework and no corresponding measure in the LEDAC Common Legislative Agenda were identified.
legislative_history: HB No. 11304 was filed in the House of Representatives of the 20th Congress on September 14, 2026 by Representative Alfred Delos Santos.
The measure is pending at the filing stage; later stages are not reflected in available records.
No earlier version, counterpart measure in the Senate, substitute bill or committee report was identified.

output.salient_features:
HB No. 11304 seeks to establish a national system of Native Flower Parks, to be overseen by a National Native Flower Parks Council attached to the DENR and financed through a Native Flower Parks Development Fund. Its salient features are as follows:
a. Section 4 (Establishment of the National Native Flower Parks Council) provides for the creation of the Council, attached to the DENR for policy and program coordination, as the principal policy-making, standard-setting and coordinating body, chaired by the DENR Secretary with the DOT Secretary as Co-Chairperson, and with members from the DOST, DA, DILG, the leagues of LGUs, the Bangsamoro Government on matters affecting BARMM, and three representatives of accredited NGOs, CSOs or POs, among others; no positions or salary grades are stated in the available text.
b. Section 5 (Functions of the Council) provides that the Council shall adopt within one year a ten-year National Native Flower Parks Development Plan, prescribe designation and accreditation standards, designate and accredit parks, maintain a National Registry, administer the Fund, accredit partner organizations, provide technical assistance and monitor park performance.
c. Section 6 (Designation and Phased Establishment of Native Flower Parks) provides that at least one Native Flower Park shall be established or designated in each administrative region within five years, with priority to areas of high endemism, lower-income LGUs, low tourism areas and geographically isolated areas, subject to LGU consent, FPIC where applicable, and site and species assessments.
d. Section 7 (Support for the Council) provides that the DENR-BMB, DOT (through TIEZA and the Tourism Promotions Board), DOST, DA, DILG, DepEd, CHED, NCIP, NCCA, the National Museum and DPWH shall support the Council within their mandates and existing appropriations.
e. Section 8 (Native Flower Parks Development Fund) provides for a trust fund administered by the Council with the DENR as depository, sourced from appropriations, a portion of the TIEZA travel tax share, park income, grants and donations, with at least sixty percent of annual disbursements applied outside the NCR.
f. Section 9 (Environmental Sustainability and Climate Resilience) provides that only native flowering plants may be planted in collection and display zones, prohibits invasive alien species, and restricts wild collection and siting in sensitive ecosystems.
g. Section 10 (Local Economic Incentives and Culturally Sensitive Approaches) provides that park employment and concessions shall favor host communities and local enterprises.
h. Section 11 (Protected Areas) and Section 12 (Linkages to Existing Projects, Initiatives, and Similar Parks) provide that the measure shall not impair protected area laws, PAMB jurisdiction or LGU authority, that participation is by voluntary accreditation, and that the Council shall first consider accrediting existing facilities before authorizing new parks.
i. Section 13 (Public Awareness Campaign) provides for a nationwide awareness campaign, declares the second week of June of every year as Linggo ng mga Pilipinong Bulaklak, integrates native flower education into curricula, and grants free admission to specified groups.
j. Section 14 (Prohibited Acts and Penalties) provides for fines of P100,000.00 to P250,000.00 for prohibited acts, with the maximum penalty imposed in specified cases.
k. Section 15 (Appropriations) provides that initial implementation shall be charged against the current year's DENR appropriations, and that subsequent funding, including annual replenishment of the Fund, shall be included in the General Appropriations Act under the DENR budget as a separate line item.
output.related_measures_policy: No related bill in the current or past Congresses was identified for HB No. 11304. The measure may be considered alongside RA No. 11038 and RA No. 7586, as amended, which govern protected areas and the jurisdiction of Protected Area Management Boards (Section 11 (Protected Areas)); RA No. 9147 on wildlife collection permits (Section 9 (Environmental Sustainability and Climate Resilience) and Section 14 (Prohibited Acts and Penalties)); RA No. 9593 on the TIEZA share in travel tax collections (Section 8 (Native Flower Parks Development Fund)); and RA No. 7160 on LGU authority over local parks (Section 12 (Linkages to Existing Projects, Initiatives, and Similar Parks)). The measure has no identified alignment with the FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework or the LEDAC Common Legislative Agenda. The review should assess whether a new inter-agency Council is needed in view of the existing mandates of the DENR-BMB, the National Parks Development Committee and the DOT, consistent with the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231), and the fiscal implications of a trust fund with a dedicated General Appropriations Act line item and a claim on travel tax collections.

Section 5 (Functions of the Council) refers to the accreditation of existing facilities 'under Section 5 of this Act', which appears to be an incorrect cross-reference.
Confirm whether the Council has a secretariat, staffing complement or member allowances, as none is evident in the provisions reviewed.

Verify the consistency of the trust fund in Section 8 (Native Flower Parks Development Fund) with the separate GAA line item in Section 15 (Appropriations) and with existing rules on special and trust funds.
Confirm with the House the current status of the bill and whether a Senate counterpart has been filed.
